money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Nicaraguan Córdoba (NIO). You can only exchange US dollars in Nicaragua. ATMs aren't always reliable. Credit cards are accepted. Contact your bank to make sure your cards will work. Using ATMs on the street puts you at high risk of robbery or express kidnapping.

consular.notes: Australia doesn’t have an Embassy in Nicaragua. The Office of the Embassy of Canada to Nicaragua provides consular assistance for Australians in Nicaragua. Australian provisional travel documents can be issued at this office. - Special travel documents (Australian Passport Office) You can also get consular assistance from the Australian Embassy in Mexico City.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include long prison sentences in local jails.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Avoid public displays of affection. Same-sex relationships are legal in Nicaragua, but the country is conservative. Same-sex marriages aren't recognised in Nicaragua.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: Nicaraguan law prohibits political activity by foreigners. Participating in demonstrations or promoting dissent, including on social media may result in you being detained or deported. It's illegal to take photos of official buildings. Check with local authorities before taking photos. If you drive a car and injure or kill someone in an accident, authorities may arrest or detain you. The local courts will need to determine who was responsible. This can take weeks or months.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: To drive in Nicaragua, you'll need either: an International Driving Permit (IDP) an Australian driver's licence You must get the IDP before arriving in Nicaragua. You also need to carry your current passport and tourist card.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Buy a tourist card at the airport, allowing a visit of up to 90 days. Nicaragua is in the CA-4 agreement with El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras: the 90 days cover land travel between the four and run from the first entry into any of them.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist card bought at the airport (CA-4, up to 90 days).
visa-preparation.before_departure: Carry a valid passport, a return or onward ticket and evidence of enough money. Smartraveller asks travellers to check with the nearest embassy or consulate before going. If routing through the US or Canada, meet their entry or transit rules.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Up to 90 days across the CA-4 countries; extend at Nicaraguan Immigration before expiry. Non-tourists or longer stays need a visa.

steps.step: Buy the tourist card at the airport on arrival, and pay the airport tax on arrival.
Show a valid passport, a return or onward ticket and evidence of enough money.
Count CA-4 days from the first entry into any member country; extend at Nicaraguan Immigration before expiry.
Check whether the Managua departure tax is in the airline ticket.
